title: Taifa of Toledo
capsule: The Taifa of Toledo was an independent Islamic principality in central Iberia that emerged after the collapse of the Caliphate of Córdoba, ruled by the Dhunnunid dynasty — a Hawwara Berber clan — from around 1018 until 1085. Toledo had been the Visigothic capital before the Islamic conquest of 711 and retained strategic centrality as the geographic heart of the peninsula; the Taifa occupied lands stretching from the Tagus valley northward toward the Duero frontier. Yahya ibn Ismail al-Mamun (r. 1043–1075) was its most capable ruler, cultivating a culturally vibrant court that attracted scholars and poets. Alfonso VI of León and Castile took Toledo without significant resistance on 25 May 1085, achieving the most significant Christian reconquest to that date and prompting the Almoravid invasion of al-Andalus.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Taifa of Toledo's general territory is attested through Arabic and Latin chronicles; its precise northeastern and southwestern frontiers with adjacent taifas are approximate, as border zones were often contested or raided rather than formally delimited.
